findings.message: A different agent (Claude) checked the work in a separate headless process.

Reviewed the Go lint config preparation, the subprocess and signal ownership, the cap on Codex PostToolUse fallback output, and the test and CI wiring. Config freezing is careful in several places. It rejects inputs it cannot preserve exactly: legacy octals, NaN, binary values, alias loops and keys that differ only by case. It defines properties safely against prototype pollution and creates temporary files with exclusive mode and random names. Each lint fallback output is capped at 16 KiB at the Codex boundary, and two parameterized tests (one with a 25,000-character warning) check that cap. I found no concrete release-relevant failure. The remaining concerns are non-blocking: lint-context size across multiple targets, signal re-raise with other listeners present, a non-discriminating cleanup assertion, and hidden-helper wiring whose source wasn't supplied.

codex-hook.ts collectPostToolLintContexts caps each target's fallback lint output at 16 KiB, but a multi-target apply_patch joins every per-target context with no cap on the total. A patch touching N Go packages can still emit about N×16 KiB of additionalContext. The 16 KiB claim is only proven for a single target.

go-lint/process.ts onSignal removes only its own listeners before calling process.kill(process.pid, signal). If any other SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP listener is still registered elsewhere in the process, Node does not apply the default termination. The re-raised signal is then swallowed and the hook keeps running after its child was killed and its temporary config removed.

In config.test.ts, the 'rejects lossy input' cases assert that no temporary file remains. Every one of those inputs fails inside parseConfig, before writeTemporary runs, so the assertion would pass even if the cleanup-on-failure path in writeTemporary were broken. That cleanup branch has no discriminating test here.

catalog.test.ts now expects 'hook go-lint' in the hidden-helper inventory, but the catalog source wasn't included in the packet. The wiring is accepted on the ledger's report of a remote correction, not verified in this review.
